newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi outlines measures to tackle trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi outlines measures to tackle trade gap.

text.p: Vietnam said on Thursday it intended setting up organisations to protect producers and traders while tightening controls on imported consumer goods as a means of tackling a ballooning trade gap.

A prime ministerial decision published in state newspapers said domestic exporters would be encouraged to deal in a wider range of commodities and form trade associations with producers to encourage production.
It said soft loans should be granted to exporters and support funds set up for producers of key commodities including rice.

The English-language Vietnam News reported that stricter controls would meanwhile be applied to imports of consumer goods through measures including closer scrutiny of turnover taxes on sales outlets and new quality controls.
Vietnam recorded a trade gap of $4.0 billion in 1996, and a $367 million deficit in January this year.

The 1996 level, a record, is equivalent to about 18 percent of annual Gross Domestic Product. In addition to causing government concern, it has stirred debate in some quarters over the merits of free trade.
But Western economists said on Thursday they were not overly concerned by the new measures.
"It's a reminder that this is not a liberal trade regime," said one. "They've had such measures before. It's really a question of how rigorously they'll be implemented."
Vietnam joined the ASEAN regional grouping in 1995 and has committed itself to lowering tariffs to between zero and five percent within 10 years.
